done: Tires & Brakes (§8.6) replaces its placeholder. It opens on the last complete lap and shows a nose-up 2x2 of corner cards (FL FR / RL RR, FRONT marker). Each card has: a tread strip with inner/centre/outer numbers on a single-hue tyre ramp; hot pressure with the cold setup value and the gain; carcass with rim; life left with this lap's wear; brake peak with mean. The hottest and most worn corner gets a lit edge and a tag, but only when it leads clearly. A lap stepper (buttons, left/right keys, "back to last complete lap") and animated numbers (reduced-motion aware) handle lap changes. A metric selector (Pressure / Tread temp / Carcass / Wear / Brake temp), also reachable by tapping a figure on a card, drives four small multiples on one shared y-scale. The new PerLapTrendChart draws mean dots on a line with a min-max band, muted laps as grey dots, and a rule on the lap the cards show. Wear uses PerLapBarChart from zero with a shared maxValue; brake temp uses the brake colour. A full per-lap table (selecting a row selects the lap) and a setup card (compound, cold pressure, camber, disc, brake balance setup vs recorded, migration, pedal force) come with it. Flat or missing channels are named in a "Not shown" note, segments for unavailable metrics are disabled, and empty, error and loading (skeleton) states are covered. The setup card sits beside the cards at >=1040 px content width and below them under that. Data layer: Corner model, multi-column lapStatsSql, readLapStatsByColumn, tireBrakeReport provider.
remaining_gaps: (1) No rubber-temperature view: the report reads carcass and rim only. Rim shows as a card caption and is not charted (it trails carcass by 1.3-9.5 C on every Sebring lap, so it adds little). (2) TyresCompound is only counted as changed or not, because its values are an undecoded index (0 on every corner of all three samples). (3) Goldens cover pressure (Sebring, 1440 px) and tread temp (Spa, 1000 px). The wear-bars, carcass and brake-temp frames are asserted structurally only, not in pixels. (4) The fixtures hold four decimals, so a fixture-fed card can print life left as 91.91 where the unrounded sample gives 91.90; tests match on substrings for that reason. (5) I did not run the live app against a real .duckdb. The compiled integration test does run the report provider end to end on the trimmed fixture. (6) The Brake Thickness channel is not drawn (flat, says '%' but holds cm); the setup's disc thickness is shown instead. (7) No Hoverable wrapper on the card figures: they use InkWell, which gives hover, focus and press states and is keyboard reachable.

data_findings:

- Sebring lap index 18 carcass means: FL 93.37, FR 83.28, RL 90.22, RR 84.95 (brief: 93.4 vs 83.3 confirmed).
- Sebring FL wear, level at lap start: 99.6328 (lap 1), 99.1675 (lap 2), 92.3484 (lap 18), 91.9050 (lap 19). Lap means 99.39 and 92.12.

- Spa Qualify: tyres start at ambient 18.0 C. RR wear goes 95.3554 to 85.7423 (-9.61) in the lap-3 spin, against 1.3-3.8 on the other corners.
- Setup: stringValue vs lastSavedStringValue differ on Sebring camber (-2.30 vs -5.00) and brake balance (51.2:48.8 vs 57.0:43.0). Brake Bias Rear = 0.4875 matches stringValue. Interlagos and Sebring VM_BRAKE_MIGRATION are 0.0; Spa is 2.5% F (event -0.025).

spec_notes: §8.6 (draft): Built in v0.11: Tires & Brakes answers two questions in the order a driver asks them. How were the tyres on that lap? Four corner cards in the car's own layout (FL FR / RL RR, nose up, a quiet FRONT marker) for a selected lap, which defaults to the last complete lap and is changed with a stepper or the arrow keys. Each card prints hot pressure beside the setup's cold value and the gain (Sebring FL 177.3 kPa, cold 136, +41.3), the tread as inner / centre / outer on a single-hue ramp with the number in every cell, carcass with rim, tread left with what the lap took (FL 91.9 %, -0.44), and brake peak with mean. The ramp spans the whole session, not the lap, so stepping laps shows real change. Inner and outer are never decided by a screen: Corner.innerEdge maps the car-frame TyresTempLeft/Right, so a left wheel's strip reads outer-centre-inner left to right and a right wheel's the reverse. The carcass leader gets a lit edge and a tag when it leads the next corner by >=0.5 C, and the most-worn corner when it leads by >=0.1 points; a garage lap at ambient crowns nobody. How did they get there? One metric at a time (Pressure / Tread temp / Carcass / Wear / Brake temp) drives four small multiples in the same layout on ONE shared y-scale. Quantities not anchored at zero use the new PerLapTrendChart (lap mean as a dot on a line, min-max as a faint band, muted laps as grey dots and whiskers off the line, a dashed rule on the lap the cards show); wear per lap uses PerLapBarChart from zero with a shared maxValue. Every charted value is also in a table (selecting a row selects the lap). A setup card carries compound, cold pressure, camber, disc thickness, brake balance (setup and recorded), migration and pedal force. The setup values come from stringValue, never lastSavedStringValue. Flat channels are named in a Not shown note, never drawn as flat lines, and disabled segments say why. tireBrakeReport reads each per-corner channel in one scan (readLapStatsByColumn, four columns, same values as four single reads, 3.4-4.6x faster). Wear per lap is the fuel view's differencing (level at lap start minus next lap start); a tyre change reads as 'tyres changed' and keeps its slot empty.\n\n§14 findings (Phase 2, Tires & Brakes): (a) Sebring Race wear per lap is 0.2295-0.5070 % on every racing lap of every corner (FL 99.63 at lap 1 start to 91.91 at lap 19 start, means 99.39 to 92.12); the clockwise circuit loads the left side: carcass FL 93.4 vs FR 83.3 C on lap index 18, FL also the most worn. (b) Inner-minus-outer tread spread is positive on every corner of every lap after the garage lap on all three samples (Sebring +6.9..+14.6, Interlagos +5.6..+11.9, Spa +3.8..+8.6 C). (c) Setup stringValue is what the car ran with: Sebring VM_BRAKE_BALANCE 51.2:48.8 matches the Brake Bias Rear event (0.4875), while lastSavedStringValue says 57.0:43.0; camber -2.30 vs -5.00 deg. (d) A Race starts on pre-heated tyres (FL first pressure 171.7 kPa against a 136 kPa cold setting), while the Spa qualifying run starts at ambient (18.0 C) and climbs lap after lap. (e) The Spa lap-3 spin is 9.61 points of rear-right wear in one lap (95.36 to 85.74) against 1.3-3.8 on the other corners. (f) Rim trails carcass by 1.3-9.5 C on every Sebring lap, so it is a caption, not a chart. (g) Brake discs swing 362-513 C inside a lap (Sebring), so brake temperature is shown in whole degrees. (h) TyresCompound holds an index the setup does not decode (0 on every corner of all three samples), so only whether it changed is used. (i) Multi-column lapStatsSql: one four-column scan is 49 ms against 225 ms for four single-column scans on 100 Hz TyresTempLeft, and 45 vs 155 ms on 10 Hz TyresPressure. Open: no rubber-temperature view; the compound index is not decoded; wear, carcass and brake frames are not in a golden.
